is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads\n a fresh token before each run, or when the issuer rejects our refres
hes, a\n stored refresh token only adds a long-lived credential. Without one, an\n expired account lists `needsReconnect: true`
and keeps its id until the next\n upload restores it.\n* **Uploads are budgeted** per person and server: 60, refilling at 120 an\

n hour. Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.

### Who can upload

An API key acts as the person who created it, wi
th all of that person's\naccess. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedicated member who\nis not a project admin, so
a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a\nserver shared with the project, accounts are project accounts: only a project\nadm

in can upload, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.

### Running evals as an account

A run wi
th no saved account choice acts as the server's **default** account.\nTo run evals from CI as one account, upload its token, make

it the default,
then start the run:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fsS -X PATCH \
 "https://app.mcpjam
.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\

" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The CLI takes the same steps with `mcpjam
cloud server-accounts set`, which\nreads the token from a file, an environment variable or stdin, and\n`mcpjam cloud server-accou

nts default`. See the
[CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-accounts-commands).

The default is
shared by every run that key starts, so don't run the same\nkey's runs at the same time with different defaults. Where your organ
ization\nhas account choice for eval suites, a suite can instead save the accounts it\nruns as, in its settings in the app; a run

with a saved choice uses those
accounts and ignores the default.

### Deleting an account

`DELETE` removes the account and i
ts stored token, and asks the token's issuer\nto revoke the token where the issuer supports revocation. That is best effort,\nand
it also ends any copy of the same token you still hold. The default\naccount can't be deleted while other accounts exist (`409`):

make another
account the default first.

### The deprecated import route

`POST .../oauth/import-tokens` still works, and is
removed 90 days after the\naccounts API shipped. It uploads to your default account, creating an unnamed\none when the server has
none, and keeps its old body and its old\n`{ imported, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carries `Deprecation: true`, a\n`Sunset`

date and a `Link` to `.../accounts`.

An account this route creates is hosted-only. An existing default it writes
into keeps wh
atever rule it had. Its `serverUrl` must be the URL saved in the\nproject, or the answer is `400`. `authorizationServerUrl`, `oaut
hResourceUrl`\nand `tokens.id_token` are accepted and ignored. Move to\n`PUT .../accounts/{account}`, which names the account it w

rites.

The error codes these routes add to `details.code` are listed in the
[error code reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/tro

ubleshooting/error-codes.md#server-account-errors).

## Run evals from the API

The shortest useful loop — create a run with o
fast on errors)\nRUN_ID=$(curl -fsS -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs\" \\\n -H \"Auth
orization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{\n \"suiteName\": \"smoke\",\n \"

serverIds": ["'$SERVER_ID'"],
 "tests": [{
 "title": "echo works",
 "runs": 1,
 "model": "anth

ropic/claude-haiku-4.5",
 "provider": "anthropic",
 "steps": [
 { "id": "s1", "kind": "prompt",

"prompt": "Use the echo tool to say hi" },
 {
 "id": "s2",
 "kind": "assert",

"assertion": {
 "type": "toolCalledWith",
 "toolName": "echo",
 "args": { "args"
failed | cancelled | timed_out\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID\" \\\n -H \"Author

ization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"

# 3. If it did not pass, read the decision summary FIRST
curl -s "https://app.mcpjam.com/ap
i/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/decision-summary\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\"\n\n# 4. Or go st
raight to per-iteration tool calls, token usage, latency\ncurl -s \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$

RUN_ID/iterations" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"
```

The decision summary composes steps 2 and 4 into on

e versioned object so every
client reads a run the same way. Four things to know before gating on it:

* **`measurementUnit` sh
ips with every count.** Under per-case grading the\n counts are case-execution *variants*, with iterations as trials inside them;
\n under a suite-wide accuracy threshold they are trials. The same suite reports\n a different total under each — 3 against 15 f

or three cases run five times —
 so a count without its unit is not a fact, and a rate is never converted
 across that line.
* **It explains the verdict; it never re-decides it.** The run's own decision is\n the authority and is carried through on `decis
ion`. The per-trial\n `diagnostics` sit underneath it — a case can pass with a failing trial in it,\n so tallying diagnostics gi
ves a different answer than the platform reached.\n* **`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a failure and not `inconclusive`.** It
\n means no verdict exists at all (unfinished, stopped early, or undecidable);\n `undecided.reason` says which. `inconclusive` *
is* a decision — the validity\n phase ran and withheld a verdict.\n* **`diagnostics.complete` says whether you have the whole lis
t.** A page\n fetched with a `cursor` is never complete, and `scannedIterations` separates\n \"nothing failed\" from \"we did no

t look".

Evidence is scoped to the claim it supports: for a measured failure the span
ids, prompt indexes and reasons come fr
om the first failed stage's row alone,\nand `evidence.tracePath` is an API-relative path you can append to your base URL\nto read

the full trace.

`model` takes an id from the hosted catalog — `provider/name` form, e.g.
`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` — and ru
ns on your organization's credits.\nProvider-native ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-key: pass\nthe key in `model
ApiKeys`. A model the API can't execute is rejected at\ncreate time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.hostedModels` lists the vali

d
hosted ids for that provider.

Reruns are even shorter: `{ "suiteId": "..." }` reruns the suite exactly as
configured, c
onnecting the suite's saved server selection (the `202` response\nlists the resolved `servers`). Pass `serverIds` to override the
selection; a\nsuite with no saved selection requires it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with\n`details.reason: \"NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION\"`

otherwise).

### Running against a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoints) is launchable only through a suite

that has
it **attached**. Attach them first with
`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}` and an `environmentIds`
a
rray (send `null` to detach them all; `[]` is rejected — use `null`), then\npass `environmentId` on the run. It must be one of tha
t suite's attached\nenvironments; anything else is a `400` with\n`details.reason: \"ENVIRONMENT_NOT_ATTACHED\"`, raised before any

case is
authored or any server connected.

Omitting `environmentId` is meaningful, and depends on the suite:

* **no** attac
hed environments → the run uses the saved server selection, as before;\n* **exactly one** attached → that environment is used auto
matically. The `202`\n response's `environment` field says so;\n* **several** attached → `400` with `details.reason: \"ENVIRONMEN

T_REQUIRED"`,
 naming the candidates.
